Materials & Methods: IZAR-2 (NCT06641089) is a 52-week multinational, randomized, double-blind, placebocontrolled, parallel-group Phase 3 clinical trial of the Nanobody sonelokimab in patients with active PsA and previous inadequate response or intolerance to 1 or 2 biologic TNFi. An estimated 600 adult patients with a confirmed diagnosis of PsA per CASPAR criteria, active disease (68 tender joint count ≥3 and 66 swollen joint count ≥3), currently active or dermatologist-confirmed historical PsO, and inadequate response or intolerance to 1 or 2 biologic TNFi will be enrolled. Patients will be randomized 1:1:1:1 to receive sonelokimab 60mg or 120mg Q4W WI (induction doses at W0, 2, 4, and 6), placebo to W16, or risankizumab given at the approved PsA dose (active reference arm; Figure). The primary outcome is ACR50 vs. placebo at W16, with key secondary outcomes (all vs. placebo) including the proportion of patients achieving ACR20, PASI 90, MDA, as well as change from baseline in the Health Assessment Questionnaire-Disability Index and Short Form-36 Physical Component Summary at W16. Risankizumab, an approved IL-23 p19i therapy commonly used in PsA after prior inadequate response to TNFi, will be the active reference arm. A key secondary endpoint will compare ACR50 responses at W16 with sonelokimab vs. risankizumab to provide additional insights into treatment choice after the failure of TNFi therapies in this population. After W16, patients receiving placebo will switch to sonelokimab 120mg Q4W WI (induction dosing to W24) until the end of treatment at W52. The IZAR-2 trial is ongoing and actively recruiting at sites across Europe and North America.
